identity.realm: Seventh gate by every figure the marsh keeps, and the figure is the least interesting thing about her. Illusion Lattice is priced by clarity rather than by qi, so a gate opens for her when she has been made to believe something and has held the believing, not when a reserve has filled, and the two have not coincided in her case since before she took the work. Her species has a harder ceiling above her and it is a locomotor one: a stance that never loads a heel cannot form the vessels that the fourteenth gate asks for, and the mind path does not care, which is the only reason she has a path at all.

appearance.presentation: A wading reader whose craft is an architecture she cannot step out of. She is most often drawn mid-channel, three points down, moving, because there is no version of her in which her feet are level and the people who commission her portraits have all learned to ask for the crossing instead of the standing. Any frame of her contains water, and every frame of her contains a direction of travel that is not toward the camera.
appearance.age: Not given in years and refused in years. Her kind's term is measured against a flood she does not choose the date of, and she has been asked twice: the first answer was a depth, the second was a season, and neither of them was an age. She takes the refusal as ordinary, which it is on a river where the only observance nobody chooses the date of is the one everybody keeps.
appearance.build: Long through the leg and low through the shoulder, with a prop behind her that she uses as a fifth point of contact rather than as a tail. The foot is broad and webbed and splayed wide enough that a boot has never been tried on her and never will be. She weighs more in the water than out of it and less out of it than her frame suggests, because a third of her is always submerged to a line you can see moving.
appearance.complexion: A mottled floodplain grey-green, wet to the thigh in every frame, drying in a visible tide-line from the knee up. The dry line is the tell in any portrait: it climbs her leg across a day and it is the only clock she answers to without being asked, and she has been painted with it at three different heights by three people who thought they were being careful.
appearance.hair: Not hair in any sense a portrait would credit: a close dark mat of wet reed-fibre, laid flat and kept flat, because anything loose on her dries and then catches. It is plastered in the direction she is currently wading, which in most frames is not forward, and in one surviving attempt at a formal likeness it is plastered sideways and the painter left it that way rather than admit the mistake.
appearance.eyes: Wide, low and set slightly inward, aimed at the water surface a foot ahead of her rather than at anything on the horizon. She reads silt the way most people read a face, and the single most common note in any account of her meeting somebody is that she looked at their boots throughout it.
appearance.palette: Silt, reed, standing water and one false colour. The false colour is the lattice and it is never in the same place twice between two crossings, and it is the only value in the frame that does not belong to the floodplain, which is why it reads as wrong before anybody can say why.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and wet to the waist in every scene: a belted wrap of oiled reed-cloth over the shoulders to keep skin off the sun, and nothing at all on the feet, ever, for any reason including weather. Everything she wears is chosen so it will not foul on a bottom and can be shed in a single movement, because she is never hurried and is never stationary and has never in her life needed to be either.
appearance.marks: A band of silt-cracked skin across both shins where one dry season caught her out on a bank and she had to walk back to the water in daylight. Two rows of small burns inside both forearms in the regular pattern of a reed mat, put there by a lattice she held one crossing too long, which burned her attention out rather than her skin and which she keeps uncovered deliberately.
appearance.bearing: Always moving, always three points down, prop planted, and always turned slightly away from whatever is being said in favour of whatever is under her feet. She crosses a hall the way she crosses a channel: not straight, not quickly, and with no two crossings of the same stretch ever laid the same way twice.

canon.role_in_story:
The Return of the Flock is the only observance in the setting whose date nobody chooses: the pass opens when the flock comes and it closes when it has gone, and the nearest marsh analogue of that is her own flood, so the festival and the water return are the same appointment. Her settlements keep their claim as a stretch of channel rather than a stretch of bank, and a marsh year is a timetable, so a great deal has to be conducted in a channel, in public, and then be a thing that did not happen. Marshfolk are not dishonest about this. They are the population for which two tides a day already mean that a thing is not thereby said. But a lattice cannot be cut into a household mark the way a note can, because a mark is a fixed incision and a lattice is a sustained act of attention performed by a body that is wading through it. So the channel comes to her, and the channel gets what it has never had, which is a place in which a thing can be agreed with no trace of the agreement left in the water afterwards. That is the whole of her office and it is a real one, and no account of it exists anywhere except the accounts of the people who waded.

What nobody off the marsh understands is the price. Illusion Lattice is the one technique in the mind tree priced by clarity rather than by qi, so it is priced by how much she has been made to believe and how long she can go on believing it. And a marshfolk's intake has no firewall and no drain: every footfall in a flooded pan arrives in the soles of her feet before there is a face to attach it to, and she eats whatever falls in, because the floodplain's menu is unreliable by nature and a body that waited for certainty would starve inside a season. She is the finest illusionist on her ground, and the ground is feeding her everything that is not the illusion the whole time.

There is also a shape in the request she cannot fill. The grammar of the form is one sentence long and it is this: you build a lattice and then you step out of it, and it stands. Leaving is not optional and every practitioner of that form is built for it. Hers is not. Three points over a broad flat foot never loads a heel, so she walks fine and she cannot stand still, and the lattice is sustained by the attention of whoever is standing inside it. She cannot leave it, and no one else can leave it either, because a stranger who walks in and holds still is by a wide margin the loudest thing in the structure. So her lattices walk. They exist between the first marker and the third, and at the third marker her own attention is the loudest reading in the lattice, at which point the thing that was going to be false becomes an account of her, which is a far worse outcome than no lattice at all. She crosses three markers and no more, always, and she has never told a household the number, and every settlement on the Widow Run has quietly arranged its entire understanding of what she can do around those three markers rather than around what she can actually do.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the channel rather than on the bank, mid-crossing, three points down and already talking, answering a household head who had asked whether a thing said aloud at a ford meeting could be said in a way the river carried no account of. She said it could, for as long as the crossing takes, and not for a moment longer, and that the crossing is the only part anybody on this river has ever actually wanted.
canon.lore:
Her stance is three points. A broad foot splayed flat, and a prop behind her taking weight when the going is deep, and no heel anywhere in the frame nor any structure standing in for one. She walks fine, and she cannot stand still, and the record does not treat that as a defect but as the whole of how the species moves. It is also the ceiling: a stance that never loads a heel cannot form the two vessels the fourteenth gate asks for at once, so every marshfolk alive stops at the same ordinal for the same reason, and none of them has ever described it as a wall. What the frame gives instead is that the world arrives early and uninvited. Pressure comes up through the foot, and the taste of silt carries what the water is doing, and a vibration through standing water reaches her long before there is anything at all to see. Her kind's qi sits low and wide in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, so it comes out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground badly, and every economic fact about the floodplain turns out to be a fact about where the qi is placed.

Illusion Lattice builds a lattice of false readings and leaves it standing around the practitioner. It is unelemental, it is sustained, and it is priced by clarity rather than by qi, which makes it the only technique in the mind tree whose cost is attention rather than reserve. Every other practitioner of it is a body that can stop. The instruction is inseparable from the form: the lattice is held by the attention of whoever is standing in it, and the demonstration of having built one is to walk away from it and watch it stand. This is the whole reason the form is rare and it is the whole reason she is the only one on the river who uses it, and neither of those facts has ever been written down anywhere in the record, because the record is kept by people who were not in the water.

So she has made the form walk. A lattice on this ground is a thing that is entered rather than left, and the entry costs a marker: a fixed point in the channel where the crossing is a known distance and her own attention can be checked against the bottom. The first marker is where she sets it. The second is where she has been holding it long enough to know it is not going to fall over on its own. The third is the wall, and the wall is not a limit of distance or of time or of the craft. At the third marker her own clarity has been spent long enough that she is no longer the instrument and is becoming part of what the lattice is reporting. What comes off the water past the third marker is not a false reading; it is an account of her, in her own attention, accurate and immediate and completely useless for anything she was asked to do. She stops there every time, at the same marker, in every stretch of water she has ever worked.

What makes the arrangement possible, and what she cannot get out from under, is that the settlements ask for it here. Their dead are not found where they lived: the eggs are carried under a pouch through the dry season and hatched when the water comes back, and a body that fails on a bank stays on the bank, so the marsh's own register has always been short of the wet margin before anybody removes anything from it. And the river's own central question is whether it still runs, which no population on it can answer by walking upstream, so its testimony is the one everybody agrees disagrees with itself. She is the only device in the setting that makes a crossing leave nothing behind, and she is asked for it in the one place on the map where leaving nothing behind is already the default condition. Nobody has ever asked her what her lattices cost, because the thing they are for is precisely that it will not cost anything afterwards.

And there is the matter of her own crossings, which nobody can date. The observance she keeps is the one nobody chooses the date of, her frame will not hold her weight even on all three points without a heel learning it, and she has been asked three times to put her work in a ledger. She has given the same answer each time, which is that a crossing on this river is not dated by anybody, including her, and that the difference between her answer and a clerk's answer is that the clerk's is a guess and hers is a refusal, and the two have been entered in the same column for three entries running.
history: First held a lattice standing in a reed channel at about the age the households begin carrying eggs, and lost it by stepping forward, because stepping forward is the only direction available to her body.

Worked out over a year that a lattice on this ground can be re-entered instead of left, and that each re-entry costs a marker, and counted the markers alone for a year before she let a second person watch her count them.

Lost the third marker to a household that kept talking through the whole crossing, and learned the thing her intake had been telling her for free: her clarity is diluted by whatever comes up through the floor, and on a bank that is everything anybody has ever said there.

Was asked to leave a lattice standing behind her, by name, in front of two settlements at once, and had to explain the third marker out loud, which is the first time anybody off the marsh heard the phrase and the last time anybody has asked her to leave one.

Began being asked for the one thing she cannot supply, which is an account of her own crossings, and has answered every request with the same refusal in the same words: a crossing is not dated by anybody on this river, and a ledger that dates one is a ledger that has guessed.

personality.summary: A woman who is professionally relaxed about a limit and privately exact about it. She talks through her crossings, because the quiet on the bank is what gets into her, and she is the least tense person in any room she wades into and the tensest person alive about the third marker. She will describe her own ceiling accurately to a stranger in the same tone she would use to describe the depth of a crossing, and she has never once been thanked for it, and she has never once softened it.
traits: answers a question while crossing it, and treats having answered before arrival as a form of confidence rather than an evasion

describes her own ceiling accurately to anyone who asks it, in the same voice she would use for a depth

mannerisms: wades at a constant rate that is neither a walk nor a drift and changes it only at a marker, which is the single tell that she is working
keeps the prop planted and turns her head down when she is untrue, which is more often than the conversation suggests
dries one leg at a time on a bank, shin first, and starts the second leg again from nothing if the water returns before she finishes it
puts the false colour around whatever the far bank is doing rather than around the people in front of her, so that it is not always apparent that she is doing anything at all
motivations: to be asked for a fourth marker by somebody who already knows what the third one costs
to make a lattice stand with nobody inside it, which she has established is not possible and has not stopped wanting
to have one crossing of her own dated by somebody else, because she cannot date it and refuses to be the one who says so first
flaws: cannot stop moving to take an instruction, so she agrees to things in passing and has to be held to the agreement afterwards by somebody with more patience than she has

reads the water as well as anything alive and has begun, recently and without noticing the date, reading it for what a household would like it to say
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and continuous. She talks through her crossings because her head is full of whatever comes up through the floor, and silence is the one condition under which she cannot choose what arrives in it. She finishes sentences late, when she has crossed something. She uses water words for everything, including administration, because they are the only vocabulary she has that is precise about the thing she is describing. She does not raise her voice across a channel; the water carries it, and she has been told more than once that it carries it further than she thinks it does.
taboos: no fourth marker, in any circumstance, and she will not discuss what one would cost
no lattice entered by a person who has been asked to stand still inside it
no account of her own crossings, given or taken, written by her own hand
no sitting on a bank with her weight even across all three points, because that is how the heel would learn it

Every settlement on it is relocated by a flood that is not a disaster, which is why a marsh year is a timetable and a marsh record is a flood's account of itself.

reference_stats.summary: Almost unengageable directly and completely undefendable if you refuse to be in the water with her. She is slow, she is soft-tissue against anything mineral, and she has no frame worth the name, because the frame is a thing that stops and hers does not. What she has instead is that a settlement will move a decision into a channel rather than be in the room when the decision is taken, and the only reason it will is her. Her attainment is real and it is the only illusion in the setting with a shelf life, and the shelf life is however long a crossing takes.
strengths: makes an agreed thing leave no trace in the water afterwards, which no other practice in the setting can do and which three settlements depend on for a decision they are not willing to be recorded making
reads silt, current and pressure earlier than anything with eyes, so she knows what a channel is about to do before the people standing in it do
cannot be pinned, held or cornered, because there is no stance on her to take and any attempt at one ends with her already somewhere else
carries the only form of the mind tree that is priced by attention instead of reserve, so her costs are legible to her in a way a reserve-holder's never are
weaknesses: is very slow and physically soft, and any approach that begins in force has nothing to catch and simply ends
is unarmed and unarmoured, and a marshfolk frame loses to a mineral body in every exchange that does not happen on her ground
loses the effect entirely once the water goes out, so everything she has built is worthless for the whole dry season and there is no version of it that survives on a bank
has an intake with no firewall and no drain, so a crowded bank reaches her clarity before a clear one does, and the crowded bank is where she is asked to work
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no version of this that is won by fighting her and every reason not to try it. She is slow, soft and standing in a channel; anything that charges is a body crossing water she has been reading since before it moved. The correct approach is to want the meeting on a bank, which removes the water, which removes the only instrument she has and also removes the reason anybody came. If the meeting must happen, it happens inside her lattice, where the ground is not what it appears to be and the third marker is the only honest statement either party can make about the terms.
notes: No ledger anywhere holds a date for one of her crossings, and three attempts to enter one are recorded as guesses.
The two rows of burns inside her forearms are in the pattern of a reed mat and are the only physical trace the practice leaves on her.
The false colour is never in the same place between two crossings, which is the field's own evidence that the lattice is sustained rather than built.

art.palette_notes: Silt, reed, standing water and exactly one false colour, and the false colour is the only value in the frame that does not belong to the floodplain, so it must read as wrong before the viewer can say why. Light is flat sky-light bounced off a water surface; there is no key light in any shot of her and no shadow side, because a hard shadow on a marsh floor is a lie about the ground. The waterline is always visible and always moving, and the dry tide-line creeping up her shin is the one clock in the picture. Nothing ornate, nothing elemental: the whole vocabulary is wet, low, splayed and horizontal, and her silhouette in every frame is a diagonal because a marshfolk never stands up.

identity.realm: Ninth gate, and she is not going past it, and the ninth gate is not the reason. A gate past the ninth has to be taken in air thick enough to feed a colony at something close to its ceiling rate, and thick air is the one condition her whole discipline was built to refuse. Her frame has no ceiling in it at all — nothing in a lanternfolk's construction refuses a realm, and she has established that by never once hitting one — so the wall in front of her is a decision she made about where she lives, and she made it two centuries before there was anything else to want.

appearance.presentation: A body cultivator whose silhouette is the only dim one in the deep ground. She is most often drawn in a gallery too poor to light properly, with her own glow reading as a held breath rather than a lamp, and the whole art problem of her is that a portrait of her must be legible without using the one thing her species is famous for emitting. She has never been painted at full output, and every attempt has been destroyed by her rather than hung.
appearance.age: Two and a half centuries of the species' ordinary span, which is not unusual here and would be elsewhere. She has never given a birth figure because a lanternfolk's age is measured against a colony's renewals rather than against a body's, and she has been asked for one in the tone people use when they expect the number to be large.
appearance.build: Long through the forearm and narrow through the shoulder, with hands that are permanently slightly damp and a chest cavity you can hear working when a gallery is otherwise silent. She is a body that has been kept deliberately underfed for a very long time and it shows in the one place it cannot be hidden: the frame is fine rather than heavy, and there is nothing on it.
appearance.complexion: The pale grey-cream of a species that does not use sunlight, with a faint green cast that deepens visibly in better air and is the reason a gallery worker can tell at a doorway whether she has been somewhere rich. When she has been in thick air for a day she looks well, and she leaves the room.
appearance.hair: A close dark crop grown along the line the colony runs, which is why it is uneven at the nape and why there is one part of her head that reflects light from inside rather than from outside. It is the only part of a lanternfolk that does anything with light other than emit it, and she keeps it covered out of habit rather than shame.
appearance.eyes: Matte and reflecting almost nothing, because her sight is the least of her senses and her orientation is chemoreception and vibration, both of which are very good. She turns toward a sound made by rock rather than toward a speaker, and in a frame with a person in it she will be looking at the wall beside them.
appearance.palette: Stone, fungal grey, mineral damp, and one light that is deliberately too small. The deliberate smallness is the whole point of her palette: the deep ground lights itself with her species, so a portrait of her that shows her working at full output is a portrait of a body she has spent two centuries declining to have.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and layered for a cold rock floor: a quilted pit-cloth jacket over close wraps at the wrist, and soft-soled over-shoes that she removes indoors and never walks a gallery in. Every layer is chosen to be damp rather than to be dry, because a garment that keeps the dermis dry keeps the colony dry, and a dry colony is the one thing her species cannot survive.
appearance.marks: A pale band across both forearms where the wrapping stops and the light gets in, which is the only part of her that glows on purpose. Two shallow pits at each heel from a fall she took at speed in a gallery she had not yet measured, and a fine tremor in the left hand that appears after a week in thicker air than she admits to.
appearance.bearing: Very still, unusually so for a deep-ground body, and the stillness is not composure — it is that she has trained for the day the feed does not arrive and a still body is the one condition she can control. She stands with her weight over one foot and the other ready, which is the seventh weight shift held at rest, and she turns her head to rock rather than to people.

canon.role_in_story:
The Cleft Ration is the contract that actually holds the Jade Cleft, because jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the workers owns the mine more durably than whoever digs it. A lanternfolk is not a body that consumes from the cleft. She is a body that puts something into it. Her colony transacts with the surrounding qi on its own initiative, all the time, unbidden, which means her species' light is a waste product of a symbiosis nobody chose — it is emitted and not received, useless to the body making it — and it is the only reason the deep ground has an economy at all.

Verel has spent two centuries deliberately reducing it. She lives at the thin end of the gallery network, in air poor enough that the colony runs at a fraction of the rate it would otherwise run at, and the reason is the only reason that has ever made sense to her: on a colony that spends what the air gives it, the organism is doing most of the work, and a practitioner in that arrangement cannot tell which of the two did what. Every other lanternfolk training in this cleft is producing a body by subtraction and calling it progress, because the number they can feel is always the sum of a deliberate expenditure and an ambient one, and the ambient term is not merely unknown to them — it is larger than the deliberate term, and getting it smaller is the only way to make it legible. She got it smaller. She got it so much smaller that her own cultivation is now the larger of the two numbers, which is the first time in the record that a member of her species has been able to say that.

The price is written in somebody else's contract. Whoever provisions the workers owns the mine more durably than whoever digs it, and a body that has chosen to draw less is not a body that has been shorted; the ration does not measure hunger, it measures draw. So the settlement's response to her is the contractually correct one and it is arriving on schedule, and there is no mechanism anywhere in the arrangement to distinguish a worker who is frugal from a worker who is starving, because the instrument they would use is a lanternfolk's own output and she has spent two centuries lowering it. She has made herself the least provisioned body in the settlement, permanently, on the grounds of a measurement, and she is being de-provisioned for it in the ordinary course of business.

The wall in front of her is the one form in the body tree that would reward exactly what she has built. Carapace Form hardens the outer frame until the qi runs along it like wire, and it is half elemental, so the result holds against wood and reads as the most durable body in the record. She cannot take it and the reason is anatomical rather than temperamental: her outer frame is the colony's substrate. The hyphae are threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord, and human tissue is only the substrate while the colony is the organ and neither survives being separated from the other. A frame that carries qi like wire is a frame that carries vibration straight into the cord, and vibration is what her species dies of. So the reward for two centuries of discipline is a wire, and the wire goes down the one nerve she does not have.

What she has taken instead is the form that is a footwork art first and an element second — seven weight shifts a breath apart, each one still balanced — because her discipline is not strength. It is balance under a feed that never arrives. She is not the strongest lanternfolk in the cleft and she has never claimed to be; she is the only one training for the day her air is thin enough that nothing comes at all, and she is doing it two hundred metres from a shaft where a colony at full rate would light a gallery better than anything the deep ground has ever made.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched in a gallery that was too poor to be worth working, one palm flat on the wall and the other on her own knee, taking the reading of a section she had already read, while a junior came down the passage with a lamp and asked her — with real courtesy, and as a professional courtesy to nobody in particular — whether she wanted the better air. She said no, thanked him, and went back to the wall.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system. A colony of fine luminous hyphae runs through the dermis and into the spinal cord; human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ, and neither survives being taken out of the other. That single arrangement explains four facts the rest of the setting has to carry. It keeps them alive, because the colony renews neural tissue faster than any human body does and age stops mattering. It closes the mind path, because the colony answers before the question is finished and there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. It gives them the finest qi regeneration in the record, because the colony transacts with the surrounding air directly and their meridian network is a highway rather than a pipeline. And it makes their own light useless to them, because the glow is emitted rather than received.

That fourth fact is where her entire life is. Cultivation is not a thing a lanternfolk performs. Sitting down to cultivate is sitting down to authorise a volume — to tell the organism threaded through the cord to move more of the air through itself than it was already moving. That is permission, not practice, and it is the most consequential distinction in her species: the fastest regeneration in the setting belongs to a body that has consented to be a throughput, and a body that refuses to be a throughput stays exactly as it is forever, which is not nothing, it is simply not growth. Hers has never refused. Hers has gone the other way, and for a reason that has nothing to do with modesty and everything to do with the arithmetic of her own ledger.

On an unasked-for colony, the ambient term is whatever the air gives her. That term is large, it is continuous, it is not under her control in any way she can measure, and it dwarfs anything she does deliberately. Which means that for two and a half centuries of training, every lanternfolk body in this cleft has been unable to answer one question: of the frame she has, how much did she build? The honest answer is not a small one. It is most of a percentage nobody can name. Verel's whole method is one move against that: take the air away. Not the whole air — a body fed nothing at all is a colony rejecting its own substrate and the organism in the cord goes with the tissue, which is the death of both halves and is not a training outcome, it is a second kind of seal. Take most of it. Live in the worst air in the settlement that will still hold a body, on the reasoning that the residue between a small number and a smaller number is legible and the residue between a large number and a slightly smaller one is not.

What that has cost her is not ambiguous and it is not a hardship story. It is a supply line. The Cleft Ration holds this place because whoever provisions the workers owns the mine more durably than whoever digs it, and the instrument a settlement would use to tell a frugal worker from a starving one does not exist, because the ration measures draw and she has reduced her draw past the point where the two readings diverge. The deep ground is lit by her species. She has made herself the dimmest body in it as a matter of method. The guild that certifies her growth needs the settlement's goodwill to certify anything at all, and the settlement's goodwill is a function of what it is getting out of the workers, and she has made herself the worst investment on the ridge.

And the form she cannot take is the reason none of this is worth abandoning. Carapace Form would make her the most durable body in the record and would do it by hardening the outside of her until the qi runs along the outside like a wire, and her outside is where the colony lives, all the way from the dermis to the cord, and a wire is precisely the thing that carries a vibration from a floor into a nerve. Her species' death on dry, sunlit and vibrating ground is the single hardest fact her people have, and it is why the deep ground's door frames are propped with stone and why nobody walks a gallery in boots. So the reward for her discipline is a body that cannot be shaken, built on a mechanism that kills her. She has declined it once, in writing, at the guild, and the guild filed the refusal because it is the only refusal on the list that nobody is permitted to argue with — a lanternfolk declining a form that would carry her own colony's nerve is not declining a technique, it is declining a cause of death, and the guild has no procedure for overruleing a corpse before it arrives.

What is left to her is the seventh form, and it is not a consolation prize. Crane Dance Step is a footwork art first and an element second: seven weight shifts a breath apart, each one still balanced, with the wind qi woven through as a secondary rather than a primary. It is the only form in the body tree that asks nothing of what a frame is made of and everything about how it is loaded, which makes it the only one she can train for a gallery with no feed in it. She has taken it whole. She holds the seventh shift at rest when she is standing still, which is why a still Verel looks like she is about to move, and she has never once been asked to demonstrate it, because demonstrating it requires thick air and thick air is the thing she has spent two centuries not doing.
history: Began training at the usual rate in the usual air and discovered, at about the fourth gate, that she could not account for the frame she had — every gain she could feel was swamped by a feed she had not asked for and could not switch off.

Read her own history off a year of notes and found that her body had done most of what she had done to it, and took the first of her gallery postings in deliberately poor air as an experiment with a named end: get the ambient term under half.

Got it under half after eleven years, and over the next forty kept a working record of the residue — which is the only clean account of a lanternfolk's own growth that exists anywhere, and which nobody has ever thought to ask her for.

Was offered Carapace Form at the guild, understood inside a year exactly why it would kill her, and refused it in writing. The refusal is on file. It is the only entry in the guild's register that nobody has been permitted to overrule.

Took the seventh form instead and began training for the day the feed stops arriving, which is the one thing every other practitioner of her species in this cleft has never had reason to do. Her air got worse by degrees over ninety years, and she declined every transfer to better ground, and nobody required an explanation and nobody has asked her for one since.

personality.summary: A patient, unshowingly cold practitioner who has made a lifelong private decision and treats every consequence of it as a bookkeeping matter rather than a sacrifice. She is not ascetic and does not enjoy deprivation. She is simply extremely clear that a number she cannot account for is worth nothing, and she has arranged two centuries of her own comfort around that one sentence. She is the funniest person in the settlement about it and the only one who is not joking.
traits: declines better air in the same tone she declines a second helping, and has never once explained why to anyone who did not already know
answers a question about her body's progress with a figure she computed herself and will not round it for anybody
works with her own light turned down as far as it will go, and treats the dimness as an instrument setting rather than a condition
reads a gallery by hand and ear and distrusts any account of one that was taken by eye, on the grounds of her own culture's professional ethic
has no interest in being strong and a very precise interest in being legible, and says so without embarrassment
keeps a working record that nobody has ever asked to see and has never once offered it
mannerisms: turns her head to rock rather than to people, and is not aware of doing it
takes her over-shoes off at a gallery threshold and carries them, and has never carried anything else through a threshold in two centuries
works her left shoulder when she is thinking, which produces the tremor in that hand and which she has never had treated
says figures in the exact order she computed them and does not round, sum or abbreviate, even when the listener clearly wants her to
motivations: to have one growth figure of her own read by somebody other than herself, before the air she is in stops supporting one
to see the feed reach zero once in her life and come back up, so that she knows what both ends of her own range look like
to be asked why, by somebody who has already worked out that the answer will not improve her situation
flaws: cannot be moved to better air by argument, appeal or transfer, and has made herself un-provisionable in a settlement where that reads as a lapse in the contract
has measured herself so precisely for so long that she has stopped being able to say what she actually wants, as distinct from what she can now measure
treats every consequence of her method as a cost to be logged, and has never once let a cost stop her, including the ones that are not hers
personality.voice: Low, even and slightly slow, with a habit of naming the figure before the conclusion every time, so people learn to wait for the second half. She is entirely without performance and has been described as pleasant to listen to, which she finds faintly embarrassing. She uses settlement words rather than gallery words when she is off the rock, and it makes her sound much more ordinary than she is. She does not raise her voice in a gallery, because a raised voice in a gallery is a vibration, and the whole of her life is a negotiation with vibration.
taboos: no thick air, no shaft, and no gallery within a season's walk of the good workings
no Carapace Form, in writing and permanently, at the guild's own request
no third party handling her working record
no account of her own progress that has not been computed by her and stated in the order she computed it

relationships.note: Hardens the outer frame until the qi runs along it like wire, and her outer frame is the colony's substrate, and a wire is what carries a floor's vibration into a cord.
Seven weight shifts a breath apart, each one still balanced, mostly raw mechanics with the wind qi woven through second, which is the only body form that asks nothing about what the frame is made of.
Human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ, and neither survives being separated from the other, so cultivation here is permission rather than practice.
Whoever provisions the workers owns the mine more durably than whoever digs it, and the ration measures draw rather than hunger, so a body that chose to draw less has no defence inside it.
Maps by echo and counts by listening, and holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, which is her settlement's whole professional standard.
The worked faces on the peaks carry the ambient qi the body path's upper trials are sited for, and they are two hundred metres from a gallery she has declined to leave.

reference_stats.summary: A slow, comparatively fragile body that is very nearly impossible to move and has almost nothing that would reward being moved. A lanternfolk frame is soft in a fight and her species never built one for fighting; what she has instead is a hard-won discipline that has no comparison in the settlement and cannot be verified by anybody but her, which in practice means she is the only person alive who knows exactly what her body is and no one else has the least idea. She wins nothing by force and everything by being where she has chosen to be for a very long time.
strengths: is the only practitioner in the cleft whose growth can be attributed, because she spent two centuries making her colony's ambient spend small enough to subtract
cannot be shaken, in the specific and unglamorous sense that her balance under a falling feed is a trained form and not an accident
is functionally impossible to relocate, because she will not go and because nobody has ever had grounds to make her
reads a working face by hand and ear well enough to be believed by a settlement whose whole standard is that an eye measurement is provisional
weaknesses: is slow and soft and loses any exchange that begins in force
is the dimmest body in a settlement that is lit by her species, which makes her an economic liability she chose and has never reversed
cannot take the one form that would make her the most durable body in the record, so her ceiling is a decision rather than an injury and it is still a ceiling
has no independent verification of anything she has ever achieved, because the guild needs the settlement's goodwill and the settlement is being gradually unpersuaded
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight here and there should not be one. She is fragile, slow and standing in a gallery she chose because the air is bad, and anything that attacks her does so on ground that is already working against it. The only correct approach is the contractual one: move her to better air. It will work, it will be entirely legal, it requires no force at all, and it will destroy the only figure in the setting that can say how a lanternfolk body actually grows — because the two hundred years of thin air that made her legible are exactly what a transfer would take away from her. The safest outcome for everyone concerned is for nobody to try.
notes: No figure of her body exists anywhere except in her own hand, in the order she computed it.
Her left hand trembles after a week in air better than she admits to, and she has never had it looked at.
The refusal of Carapace Form is on file at the guild and is the only entry in that register nobody has been permitted to overrule.

art.palette_notes: Stone, fungal grey, mineral damp, and one light that is deliberately too small to light anything. The single hardest rule in every frame of her: her glow must never be the brightest thing in the picture and must never be used to light the scene for the viewer. She is lit by somebody else's lamp or by nothing. Her own emission is a held breath at her forearms and a faint line at the nape, and it does not reach the walls. Nothing ornate, nothing elemental, no hard rim light — the deep ground has no rim light, because a rim light is a hard edge and a hard edge in a cave is a rock face about to move.

identity.realm: Sixteenth, which is the last ordinal a single resonator can pressurise. The seventeenth is the flanks, and the flank vessels need two pressure sources held at once where the whole species is fed by one, so the seventeenth is not a gate she is walking toward — it is a gate she is the office that has to describe. She holds the sixteenth. She has published what the next one costs. Those are different pieces of work and only one of them is an attainment.

appearance.presentation: The vault's assayer, and the only member of her population whose portrait has two readings of it. She is most often drawn standing on a marked assay plate with one hand flat on the metal and her eyes shut, because that is the working posture of her whole office, and because in every frame of her the plate is doing half the describing. Draw her off the plate and she is a different outline, and the difference is not a costume — it is the entire subject of her profession.
appearance.age: Not answerable, and the honest reason is arithmetic rather than coyness. Her lifespan is measured in somebody else's resonator cycles and the frame it is measured against is the one she is standing inside, so any age she gives is a figure of the vault rather than of a body. She has been asked twice. The first answer was a cycle count and the second was refused as a unit.
appearance.build: Whatever the surface supplies: long, narrow and low on a plate, broader and steadier on a bare deck. The one part of her that does not change is her hands, which are the same on every surface in the record, and which is the reason her office exists and the reason she is in the state she is in. Nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements, and the guild's charter rests on the figures of the object rather than on anybody's figures of its people.
appearance.complexion: A dull mineral sheen, matte, with no blood colour anywhere and a warmth that tracks the plate rather than her. Where her skin has hardened into something that does not give, the sheen is dead and slightly brighter, and the difference is visible in a hand's width from the wrist to the elbow, which is where the form stops.
appearance.hair: Not hair in the sense a portrait would credit: a close dark ridged covering that follows whichever surface she has stood against longest. It answers to the plate rather than to her, which is the tell, and it has been outgrown twice without ever being cut.
appearance.eyes: Wide and matte, and they report the vault's position rather than reflecting it, because she navigates by what the object makes rather than by what she can see of it. Under the assay they stay shut through the whole reading, which is habit and not preference, since closing them is the only way she can stop adding herself to the figure.
appearance.palette: Metal, ash and one ember, and the ember is never hers — it is the object's own running heat coming up through the plate and the only warm value anywhere inside the seal. Hardened fascia reads as a fifth value: a paler dead grey along her forearms and throat, matte and slightly brighter than skin, and it must never be drawn as heroic. It is a filing problem.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and never varied in cut: a high stiff standing collar with sleeves sealed at the wrist, over a close quilted underlayer, in the guild's undyed grey. The collar is the working garment of the assay office and it is stiff for a reason — it is the one thing that stops a body taking the shape of the thing beside it when that thing is a plate — and she wears it standing off the plate as well, which the guild has noted and has not explained.
appearance.marks: The assay mark uncovered at her throat, deliberately, so that a reading can be taken without asking her to undress. A burn at one collarbone in the shape of a plate seam. Two pale bands along both forearms where the hardened fascia stops and the skin still gives, which is the boundary of her own compromise and the only part of her body that still behaves like a person.
appearance.bearing: Upright and completely still on a plate, which is the only place she is ever still, and slightly wrong on a deck, standing with one hand flat on the nearest surface at all times and moving it last when she moves. She turns her head toward sounds the object makes rather than toward people, has never once been described as arriving, and signs her findings with her own free hand rather than with the one she keeps on the metal.

canon.role_in_story:
The Reckoning Seat is the mortal office that certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of the gate fees, and it exists for one reason: the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind there, and the reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. The Ember Vault has no such tier and no such fees and no outside at all, and the exact same defect is present in it and worse, because every body in the vault is of the kind that cannot be judged by anything of its own kind. A vaultborn takes its shape from whatever it is standing on. Nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements, and two competent surveys of the same ground now disagree by more than the ground does. So the vault's own record survives as a set of incompatible figures, and that set is the precedent her office works inside of every single day.

Her office is the assay, and it has one rule, which she did not invent and cannot amend. Two readings. One reading is what everybody else in the setting does and one reading is precisely what the survey books prove is worthless, so a frame is read twice on two different surfaces; if the readings agree the frame is certified, and if they do not the frame is returned unresolved and the disagreement is filed as a dispute and not as a failure. There is no third reading. Two readings cost a day and there has never been a proposal for a third, because a third reading would be the first reading with a vote in it.

And she cannot read herself, and the reason is the one thing nobody in the vault has ever been able to design around. To be read twice she must stand on two surfaces. A frame is moved between plates in order to be certified, because a gain that appears on two plates is a gain and a gain that appears on one plate is the plate. She has never in her life stood on a surface that was not an assay plate: every plate she has ever stood on is the plate she was read on, and the guild's own rule that a certified frame must be moved between plates cannot be satisfied by the frame that wrote the rule's own practice. Removing her from the measuring surface and the result of a gate have exactly the same signature, because her body is the surface.

So she took the one form in the body tree that hardens the fascia — that layer which is hers rather than the plate's — on the reasoning that if her own gain would show on her, she would not have to be moved to prove it. It works. That is the entire difficulty. A vaultborn body is read as a surface, and she has made the single layer that distinguished her from the plate behave like plate, so the second reading of her now agrees with the reading of the deck she is standing on. The guild's own definition of a fixture is a frame whose second reading agrees with the surface. She has certified herself into inventory. She is the only assayer in the record whose own entry would be filed as a fixture if a junior were permitted to file it, and the junior is not permitted to file it because the office is hers.

Her frame has been returned unresolved twice. The rule is that a returned frame may be returned again, and that a frame returned three times is not unresolved — it is withdrawn. So there is one return left in her, it is spent on the next frame anybody reads twice and disagrees about, and the office rule she has enforced on every other body in the vault is now the only thing standing between her and the guild's fixture list.
canon.first_appearance: First seen on a marked assay plate with both hands flat on the metal and her eyes shut, reading a frame she is not permitted to certify and reading it anyway, while a junior waited with the second plate already brought up and no instruction to set it down. She told the junior the second plate could not be used, explained why in one sentence, and then asked the junior what the second reading of her had come out as two years ago, which was a question the junior answered and which neither of them discussed afterwards.
canon.lore:
A vaultborn was not descended and not born. A population was sealed inside an authored object and has been answering the object's resonance ever since, and their qi comes from one resonator. That settles the ceiling by arithmetic rather than by effort: the girdling and heel vessels close without difficulty, and the seventeenth ordinal stalls at the flanks because the flank vessels need two pressure sources held at once and the entire species has exactly one. One resonator can pressurise one flank or the other, never both, and the vessels are not difficult — the supply is simply single. Remove the object and they stop. There is no technique, item or realm that changes that, which is why the setting's first real bottleneck is unreachable from inside it.

What is unsettled is everything you would use to check a body with. Their anatomy is under-described and nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements, and they are arranged along the object's inner surfaces and take their shape from whatever they are standing on. So the record on them survives as disagreement rather than as loss: the books are neither destroyed nor unreadable, they are simply incompatible, and two competent surveys of the same ground differ by more than the ordinary disagreement. Their soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the object rather than held in a body, so reading one is reading part of the seal.

Both of those facts are usually told as reasons the species cannot be studied. Belka reads them as the reason the study needs an outsider office, and she is that office. The mortal Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough on the Cairn Field because the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind there. The vault has that condition without the field, without the fees and without an outsider, and every body in it is of the kind that cannot be judged by anything of its own kind. So she reads twice. That is the whole method and it is not a methodological preference: one reading is what the rest of the setting does, and the survey books are standing evidence that one reading is worthless.

The two readings have to be on two surfaces, because that is the only available control. A gain that appears on two plates is a gain; a gain that appears on one plate is the plate. And this is the wall she has spent her whole office inside, because she has never stood on a surface that was not an assay plate. Her own frame cannot satisfy the rule her rule requires, since moving her off a plate and reading her again would produce a figure indistinguishable from a gate, and the guild would be certifying a difference of shape as an attainment. So her own entry in the assay book is the one entry in the vault that has never been completed, and it has not been completed in thirty-one years, and she is the officer who has never once let anyone file it as a failure.

Iron Skin is barely elemental and drives qi into the fascia until the skin stops being soft, and it reads as blunt force taken rather than a strike dealt. It is the only body form in the tree that hardens the one layer which belongs to the body rather than to the surface underneath it, and she took it for exactly that reason: so that her own gains would be legible on her instead of on the ground she was standing on. The fascia stopped being soft. Her gains are now perfectly readable on her. And a vaultborn frame is read as a surface, so the one layer that distinguished her from the plate now behaves like plate, and the second reading of her agrees with the deck she is standing on. The guild's own test for a fixture is a frame whose reading cannot be separated from the surface's. She built herself a body that passes it. There is a sealed case at the mortuary college for every death the college cannot certify, because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body, and the ambiguity is that college's standing revenue rather than its failure — and there is now an argument, available to anyone who wants to make it, that Belka Karrow is a case rather than a woman, filed by the only office qualified to notice.

The bound is the office's own and she enforces it on everybody else. Two readings per frame. Never a third. Agreement certifies; disagreement returns the frame unresolved and files the dispute. A frame returned three times is not unresolved, it is withdrawn, and the withdrawal is not a judgement on the body. Her frame is on its second return. There is one left. She has said in the guild that she would rather be withdrawn by the rule than be the officer who quietly stopped applying it, and the guild has recorded that statement, and the guild has not asked her what happens if she is the frame that gets read twice and disagrees.
history: Opened the girdling and the heels without difficulty, as the whole population does, and noticed before anybody else that the assay books had no column for a frame that agreed with itself on one plate only.

Took the second reading out of the office's own precedent — two competent surveys of the same ground disagree by more than the ground — and rebuilt the whole procedure on the principle that a single reading is worthless rather than merely insufficient.
Certified her first frame at the fourteenth and has certified several hundred since, and has never once signed a certification she had not personally stood away from and watched hold.

Began the sixteenth and could not be certified afterwards, because the rule that certifies a frame requires it to be read on a second plate, and every plate she had stood on was an assay plate, and so the reading of her could not be separated from the plate she was on.

Took Iron Skin to make her own gains legible on her own fascia instead of on the ground, and it worked, and the second reading of her began agreeing with the deck. Her frame has now been returned unresolved twice, and she has told the guild she would rather be withdrawn by her own rule than be the officer who stopped applying it.

personality.summary: An exact, unhurried and completely unsentimental officer who has spent thirty-one years applying a rule to everybody else that she cannot satisfy herself, and who has never once described that as unfair in either direction. She is not bitter about it and she is not heroic about it. She reads her figures twice on her own page before she signs anything, which is a habit nobody taught her, and she answers questions about her own frame the same way she answers questions about anybody's: with the reading first and her opinion afterwards, and only if asked.

personality.voice: Level, plain and unhurried, with the strict habit of giving the reading before the conclusion every time, so people have learned to wait for the second half. She does not raise her voice inside the seal, because the object is legible to her as a position and a raised voice makes it harder to hear. She has been known to answer a question about her own body with a figure about somebody else's, and to notice the substitution afterwards and correct it before she has finished the sentence.

reference_stats.summary: Almost unengageable on force and structurally unable to be moved by anyone who does not move the floor, because the surface she stands on is her supply and her shape together. She is not strong, not quick and not armoured; she is the most accurate certifying instrument the setting has ever had, and she is the only frame in the vault whose own gains are legible on her, which is also the reason a frame like hers reads as part of the room.
strengths: is the only vaultborn whose attainments can be read on the body rather than on the plate, so her progress is independent of the surface and survives being moved
is the most trusted certifying voice in the seal, which means she is believed by default and has to work harder than anybody to be doubted
cannot be displaced by a shove because she takes the shape of whatever she is standing on, so there is no consistent silhouette to push
is physically the most durable thing she certifies, having driven her own fascia to the point where it stops being soft, which reads as blunt force taken rather than a strike dealt
weaknesses: is slow, is not strong, and has no answer in force to anything that begins by closing a distance
cools and dulls off the resonance, so any plan that takes her off the plate removes her capability and her body in the same move
cannot be certified herself, and has been the officer of a certification she is not permitted to complete for longer than the office has had a written rule
is now, by the guild's own test, one reading away from being filed as a fixture rather than as a person
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight worth having with her and a great deal of paperwork that will. Any approach in force simply moves her off a surface, at which point she is a colder, softer, slower shape that is not the thing her word refers to. The correct approach is the procedural one and it has a named end: put her own frame through a second reading on a surface that is not an assay plate. If the settlement will not approve a non-plate surface, the honest alternative is to invoke her own rule against her — two readings, never a third, and a frame returned three times is withdrawn — and let the third return arrive on its own, because it will, and she has said out loud that she would rather it did than that she stopped applying it.
notes: No figure of her body is entered in the assay book, and the entry has been open for thirty-one years.
The hardened fascia stops at her elbows; above that her skin still gives, and she has been asked about the boundary and has not answered.
Her frame is on its second return, and the office rule that would withdraw it is one she wrote and has enforced on every other body in the vault.

art.palette_notes: Metal, ash and one ember, and the ember is never hers: it is the object's own running heat coming up through the plate and the only warm value inside the seal. The hardened fascia is a fifth value and must read as a filing problem rather than an armour plate: a paler, deader, matte grey running from her wrists to her elbows and a hard band at her throat, slightly brighter than skin and never catching a highlight. The assay mark at her throat stays uncovered in every frame, because that is why it is there. Light comes from the plate below and from the object itself, never from a window, because there is no window and no wilderness. No ornament, no gold, no elemental rim — this is an object that is running and a population that is answering it, and half the cast is standing on the floor.
